extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of electric utilities and independent power producers; permitting authorities; environmental regulators; environmental attorneys and consultants; commenters on CCR rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria, definitions, thresholds, and procedural requirements the EPA sets forth for identifying, regulating, and permitting CCR management units (CCRMU) under RCRA, including applicability, required monitoring/closure obligations, and owner/operator responsibilities. Focused on how the final rule applies to different categories of CCR placements and what obligations/responses are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability threshold — CCRMU ≥ 1,000 tons
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart applies to CCR management units of 1,000 tons or greater, located at facilities with a regulated CCR unit or active facilities without a regulated CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only CCRMU containing 1,000 tons or more of CCR are required to comply with the applicable requirements for CCRMU after the effective date of this rule (§257.50(d)(1)). The threshold is based on the Agency's risk analyses and authority under RCRA section 4004(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim scope — CCRMU ≥ 1 ton and < 1,000 tons (FER-only until permitting determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCR management units greater than or equal to 1 ton and less than 1,000 tons, located at facilities with a regulated CCR unit or active facilities without a regulated CCR unit, are only subject to the requirements of the facility evaluation report in §257.75 until a permitting authority determines that regulation of these units, either individually or in the aggregate, is warranted and determines the applicable requirements (§257.50(d)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment of these smaller units is deferred to permitting authorities who will assess risks posed individually and/or in aggregate. Facilities must identify these smaller units as part of the FER so the information can be submitted in permit applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling limitations informing thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA modeled individual placements of CCR between one ton and 78,000 tons but did not model below one ton and conducted too few model runs at smaller amounts to support extrapolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because EPA could not identify a precise tonnage below which there is no reasonable probability of adverse effects, the Agency set thresholds consistent with available risk analyses (resulting in the 1,000-ton applicability threshold). EPA noted that groundwater concentrations from individual quantities below one ton are very unlikely to exceed GWPSs, but could not determine an exact safe limit between one and 1,000 tons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate-risk consideration for multiple smaller CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA acknowledges that while individual small CCRMU may not exceed levels of concern, aggregate risks from multiple small CCRMU co-located at a facility may be meaningful and could increase overall risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA modeled individual units rather than aggregate placements; permitting authorities are expected to consider aggregate impacts when deciding to regulate smaller units. Facilities continue to monitor regulated units and larger CCRMU; aggregate contributions from smaller unmonitored units should become apparent through ongoing monitoring and corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify smaller units in Facility Evaluation Report (FER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule requires facilities to identify CCRMU containing between one and 1,000 tons as part of the FER so that this information can be submitted as part of their permit application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification in FER enables permitting authorities to assess individual and aggregate risks and determine appropriate requirements. Owners/operators must include these units in the FER even if regulation is deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subset of part 257 requirements extended to CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule extends only a subset of the existing requirements in part 257, subpart D to CCRMU: groundwater monitoring, corrective action, closure, post-closure care, and recordkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective action is required only if triggered by site-specific determinations particular to individual units. The rule does not extend the full suite of subpart D requirements to CCRMU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action triggered by site-specific determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrective action for CCRMU is required only if triggered by site-specific determinations particular to individual units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will not impose blanket corrective action on all CCRMU; site-specific monitoring and assessment will determine when corrective action is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficial use exemption — limited to off-site beneficial use
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the existing regulations, CCR that is beneficially used off-site is not a CCR pile; direct placement of CCR on the land on-site of a utility, with nothing to control releases, is by definition a CCR pile and therefore not beneficial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second sentence of §257.53 limits beneficial use of CCR to 'off site.' Activities that meet the regulatory definition of beneficial use are not considered disposal, even if they involve on-the-ground placement of non-containerized CCR off-site as part of beneficial use. The final rule does not alter this distinction; EPA declines to reconsider the existing definition of CCR pile in this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'CCR pile'
rubrics_metrics.description: CCR pile: 'Any non-containerized accumulation of solid, non-flowing CCR that is placed on the land. CCR that is beneficially used off-site is not a CCR pile.' (§257.53)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-site non-containerized CCR that is not in the process of being beneficially used constitutes disposal and is regulated as a CCR pile (and thus a CCR landfill) under current rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for roadbeds and associated embankments
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing an exemption for CCR used in roadbeds and associated embankments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility later determines that the CCR in an onsite roadbed is contributing to contamination of the aquifer, the facility would be required to address the contamination as part of ongoing remediation. EPA amended the CCRMU definition to reflect this exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions must avoid circularity — clarity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters objected to circular definitions (e.g., 'CCR unit', 'CCR landfill', 'CCRMU' defined by reference to each other). EPA agrees revisions are necessary to avoid circularity and clarify essential characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule relies on distinct definitions for three terms—'CCR unit', 'Regulated CCR unit', and 'CCR management unit'—and adds clarifying sentences (e.g., 'This term includes both Regulated CCR units and CCR management units') to reduce ambiguity about what is in/out under 40 CFR part 257, subpart D.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'CCR unit' definition — broad encompassing term
rubrics_metrics.description: 'CCR unit' means any CCR landfill, CCR surface impoundment, or lateral expansion of a CCR unit, or a combination of more than one of these units, based on context. This term includes both Regulated CCR units and CCR management units (section 257.53).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA largely reverted to the existing 2015 definition and explicitly stated that the term includes both regulated and management units, making it the broadest term under part 257, subpart D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Regulated CCR unit'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Regulated CCR unit' refers to the units regulated by the 2015 CCR rule, i.e., new CCR landfills and new CCR surface impoundments (including lateral expansions), existing CCR landfills, existing CCR surface impoundments, inactive surface impoundments at active facilities, and legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This term identifies units subject to the full requirements of the 2015 CCR rule and helps minimize revisions to existing regulatory text by grouping those units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'CCR management unit' (CCRMU)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCR management unit means any area of land on which any noncontainerized accumulation of CCR is received, is placed, or is otherwise managed, that is not a regulated CCR unit. This term includes inactive CCR landfills and CCR units that closed prior to October 19, 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA deleted the phrase 'at any time' to avoid confusion. 'Closed prior to October 19, 2015' is defined to mean the unit completed closure under state law prior to that date. CCRMU are the units subject only to the subset of requirements (groundwater monitoring, corrective action, closure, post-closure, recordkeeping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair notice/due process requirement for regulatory clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must give regulated entities 'fair notice' of conduct that is forbidden or required; definitions and thresholds must provide ascertainable certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued that the proposed CCRMU definition lacked clear criteria (e.g., how much non-containerized CCR triggers regulation). EPA addressed by codifying thresholds in §257.50(d) and revising definitions to provide clearer regulatory text rather than relying solely on preamble statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCRA section 1006(a) interpretation on anti-duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: RCRA section 1006(a) does not bar EPA from imposing requirements under RCRA and another listed statute (e.g., CWA) on the same units and waste streams unless those requirements are inconsistent with a requirement in one of the statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA cites statutory language and case law (e.g., Chemical Waste Management v. EPA; Ecological Rights Foundation v. PG&E; Goldfarb v. Baltimore; Edison Electric Institute v. EPA) to support the interpretation that overlapping regulation is permissible unless there is a specific inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of historical/legacy placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities characterized as 'historical' (e.g., structural fill and CCR placed below regulated units on-site) were treated as disposal under the 2015 CCR rule and remain regulated as such; EPA declines to reconsider the CCR pile definition that covers historical on-site permanent placements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assumes facilities complied with existing requirements historically; the rule does not reopen prior determinations about those activities in this rulemaking, absent specific proposal and solicitation for comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner definition revised to include CCRMU and facility-level ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'Owner' is revised to include owner(s) of CCR management units and the owner(s) of the entire facility, whether in whole or in part (i.e., add 'or CCR management unit' and 'or a facility, whether in whole or in part').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision accounts for complex ownership where individual units or portions may be owned by different entities; EPA expects most utilities already operate as if required owners/operators must act. EPA recognizes potential access and liability complexities and extended deadlines to accommodate access issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator definition revised to account for CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Operator' is revised to incorporate CCRMU by including persons responsible for disposal or otherwise actively engaged in solid waste management of CCR and those responsible for directing or overseeing groundwater monitoring, closure, or post-closure activities at a CCR unit or CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA clarifies the revision is intended to follow standard 'operator' liability under environmental regulations and is not intended to include every person or contractor involved; EPA provides guidance that typical regulatory practice treats compliance by one responsible entity as satisfying obligations for all potentially liable parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability allocation guidance between owners and operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided in the regulations, as long as one responsible entity (an owner or operator) has complied with the requirements, EPA will consider the obligation satisfied as to all potentially liable parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will initially rely on owners and operators to determine among themselves how best to ensure compliance. This is consistent with prior EPA practice (e.g., 45 FR 33295).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming revisions to related definitions to include CCRMU where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed adding 'or CCR management unit' to eight definitions in §257.53 (Active life or in operation, Active portion, Closed, CCR landfill or landfill, Qualified person, Qualified professional engineer, State Director, Waste boundary) to incorporate CCRMU; it is finalizing some conforming changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the final CCR unit definition was revised, not all seven of these definitions needed amendment; EPA finalized proposed revisions to CCR landfill and State Director and handled other conforming changes as described in the preamble and Volume II Response to Comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of regulated facilities — active facilities and inactive facilities with at least one CCR unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule requires owners/operators of active facilities with one or more currently regulated CCR unit(s) and inactive facilities with a legacy CCR surface impoundment to comply with CCRMU regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters urged broader coverage (e.g., units at currently unregulated active facilities), but EPA limited the regulated universe to the categories above consistent with statutory authority and the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment exposure scenario — future residential use
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's modeled radiation risks of concern at lower quantities were based on a future residential use of the property (e.g., after clean closure of the regulated units, but where smaller CCRMU remain on site).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA acknowledges current (occupational) exposures at existing facilities differ from the modeled future residential scenario; commenters raised this distinction in comments on the risk assessment.
